messages.content:
Given a question and an answer, analyze the complexity of each sentence in the answer. Break down each sentence into one or more fully understandable statements. Ensure that no pronouns are used in any statement. Format the outputs in JSON.
Please return the output in a JSON format that complies with the following schema as specified in JSON Schema:
{"properties": {"statements": {"description": "The generated statements", "items": {"type": "string"}, "title": "Statements", "type": "array"}}, "required": ["statements"], "title": "StatementGeneratorOutput", "type": "object"}Do not use single quotes in your response but double quotes,properly escaped with a backslash.

--------EXAMPLES-----------
Example 1
Input: {
    "question": "Who was Albert Einstein and what is he best known for?",
    "answer": "He was a German-born theoretical physicist, widely acknowledged to be one of the greatest and most influential physicists of all time. He was best known for developing the theory of relativity, he also made important contributions to the development of the theory of quantum mechanics."
}
Output: {
    "statements": [
        "Albert Einstein was a German-born theoretical physicist.",
        "Albert Einstein is recognized as one of the greatest and most influential physicists of all time.",
        "Albert Einstein was best known for developing the theory of relativity.",
        "Albert Einstein also made important contributions to the development of the theory of quantum mechanics."
    ]
}
-----------------------------

Now perform the same with the following input
input: {
    "question": "user: How much is the fee to get a copy of the oral argument recording from the court?\nassistant: I do not have that information. \nuser: Can anyone pay a fee to get a copy of an oral argument recording from the court?\nassistant: Yes. Any party may pay a fee to get a copy of their oral argument recording from the court.\n\nuser: When you say \"any party,\" it refers to the individuals involved in the case, not the general public, correct?\nassistant: Yes, that's correct. In the courts, the individuals or entities directly involved in the case are referred to as parties; for example, ask for the name of party.\nuser: Who makes the oral arguments?\nassistant: To be eligible for an oral argument, a party must have filed a brief that has been accepted by the Court of Appeal. If the respondent did not file a brief, they cannot make an oral argument. If a party is represented by a lawyer, the lawyer will present the oral argument. A party is not required to attend court for the oral argument if they have legal representation. The court will provide all parties with at least 20 days' advance notice, which will include the date, time, and location of the oral argument.\nuser: Can I decline to participate in an oral argument?\nassistant: Yes. You have the option to decline to participate in an oral argument. If you decide not to make an oral argument, it will not affect the court's view of your arguments in the appeal. Not all parties are required to participate in the same way; if only one party wishes to present an oral argument, the court will hold the oral argument for the case but will not compel the other parties to participate. \nMany appeals do not include oral arguments because all parties choose to waive (give up) their right to do so. When there is no oral argument, the Court of Appeal justices decide based solely on the written briefs and the appeal record. It is important to note that oral arguments do not speed up or delay the appeal process.\nuser: Good to know. \nassistant: Is there anything else I can help you with?\nuser: Can I have the fees waived?",
    "answer": "You can request a fee waiver, and if approved, the court will generally waive most—but not all—fees. However, page 1 does not specify whether the fee for a copy of an oral argument recording can be waived, so I cannot confirm that this particular fee is covered."
}
Output:

statements: A party can request a fee waiver from the court.
If the fee waiver request is approved, the court will generally waive most fees.
An approved fee waiver does not cover all court fees.
Page 1 does not specify whether the fee for a copy of an oral argument recording can be waived.
The assistant cannot confirm whether a fee waiver covers the fee for a copy of an oral argument recording.
